create.title: Exact diagonal gamma factorization and single-transition normal forms
create.statement_tex: With alpha=Im s+Im(u+v)/2 and beta=Im s-Im(u+v)/2, K_z(1-s) factors exactly into R_alpha R_beta times the explicit 2,pi powers, where R_alpha=Gamma((1+sigma+zeta/2)/2+i alpha/2)/Gamma((2-sigma-zeta/2)/2-i alpha/2) and R_beta=Gamma((sigma-zeta/2)/2+i beta/2)/Gamma((1-sigma+zeta/2)/2-i beta/2). If beta is bounded and alpha large, R_beta remains exact while R_alpha has power |alpha/2|^(sigma+zeta/2-1/2) and signed Stirling phase |alpha|log(|alpha|/2)-|alpha|+pi/4; the opposite transition interchanges alpha,beta and has phase constant -pi/4. The map (t,eta,mu) to (alpha,beta,nu) has absolute Jacobian one and sends the finite box to |nu|<=V, |alpha-beta-nu|<=U, |alpha+beta|<=2S. All profiles, residues, stars, and horizontal sides remain explicit.
create.next_action: Use this normal form for signed transition estimates; do not replace the bounded gamma factor by large-argument Stirling.

create.title: Absolute nested contour exhaustion cannot remove the hard radial sides
create.statement_tex: For S=(X+U+V+2)^4, radial horizontal sides are separated from both gamma transition planes and the radial x-phase is nonstationary. Because the finite radial cutoff is hard, integration by parts produces endpoint terms beginning at O(S^(-1)), not rapid decay. On the forced left edge lambda=1-c'<0, the available degree-two functional-equation upper capacity is O(S^(1-2lambda)); hence the elementary absolute side bound is O(S^(-2lambda)), which grows. On terminal single-transition traces, the gamma power combined with the hard 1/u profile is likewise not absolutely integrable. This rules out side deletion and transition control by absolute pointwise estimates or faster nesting alone; it does not rule out a new signed boundary or vector-Hilbert cancellation theorem.
create.next_action: Subtract explicit radial endpoint asymptotics before contour shifting and test signed cancellation of the resulting boundary functional.

create.title: Renormalized radial endpoint and diagonal vector-Hilbert operator
create.statement_tex: Expand G_v(w) at both hard radial endpoints to sufficient finite order, subtract those endpoint asymptotics before the radial contour shift, and retain the resulting explicit boundary functionals together with every zeta, height, hard-Perron, corner, and radial endpoint residue. Prove that the renormalized radial horizontal sides vanish under a declared nested exhaustion and that the remaining two diagonal single-transition traces satisfy a target-sized signed vector-Hilbert estimate under the symmetric top 1/u limit. No absolute-value or fixed-order shortcut is allowed.
create.next_action: Derive the endpoint subtraction algebra exactly and test whether its boundary terms pair with existing residues before attempting the transition estimate.

update.statement_tex: In diagonal heights alpha=Im s+Im(u+v)/2 and beta=Im s-Im(u+v)/2, control both exact single-transition normal forms together with the radial horizontal-side functional and all residues. Absolute nested exhaustion fails because hard radial endpoints give only S^(-1) decay against functional-equation growth; the next sufficient interface is M9-M1-renormalized-radial-boundary-operator.
update.next_action: Renormalize radial endpoint expansions and seek signed boundary/residue cancellation plus a vector-Hilbert estimate on both transition traces.

reject.reason: Hard radial endpoint terms decay only as S^(-1), while the left-edge functional-equation factor has growing polynomial capacity.
On a swept trace the one-large gamma power combined with the hard 1/u measure is nonintegrable on the required terminal abscissa.
The normal form supplies exact phase and amplitude but no signed vector-Hilbert or boundary cancellation estimate.
The stronger claimed two-sided asymptotic lower bound for the full side functional did not receive the planned hostile validation; only the absolute-method capacity obstruction is accepted.
